markdown_report:
**Synthesis.** Three starting-point insights motivate a small SASRec extension. (1) Causal attention already represents changing interests. A residual can test a specific weakness while retaining that backbone. (2) The supplied simulator diagnosis distinguishes repeated narrow preferences from isolated actions. Additional preference reinforcement should therefore depend on preceding evidence. (3) Electronics has 14.95% wrong rankings and margin p10 −0.4812. These training diagnostics motivate improving separation but do not establish validation performance.

Three literature insights constrain the experiment. (1) [gSASRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.07192) supports testing multi-negative objectives. It does not identify the cause of this task’s errors. (2) [HyperHawkes](https://evazangerle.at/publication/peintner-www-2025/) separates recurring interests and short-term activation. This motivates retrieving relevant history without averaging competing interests together. (3) [Recformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13731) and [SCRM](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.14957) use resources or behavior distinctions unavailable here. Their results cannot establish scratch-text gains or verified complementarity under this contract.

**Framework and directions.**

| Direction | Existing mechanism | Proposed experiment | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Temporal evidence | SASRec; prior pooled residual | Recent-anchor history retrieval | Similarity is not intent truth |
| Ranking objective | gSASRec | Multi-negative gBCE | No direct practical-utility mechanism |
| Interest persistence | HyperHawkes | Three causal interest slots | Assignment and optimization cost |

**Candidate assessment.** Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each entry gives a positive and negative reason.

- **A: Support-gated recent-anchor retrieval — 4/7/8/7/4.** Originality: query-specific pooling / attention precedent. Potential: reusable evidence mechanism / embedding feedback. User alignment: recent narrow matches and restrained extrapolation / no compatibility knowledge. Model alignment: candidate margins change / gains unproven. Difficulty: tensor features retained / causal indexing needs care.
- **B: Multi-negative gBCE — 2/7/4/9/3.** Originality: task adaptation / established objective. Potential: inexpensive ranking intervention / dataset dependence. User alignment: stronger competition / no explicit intent support. Model alignment: targets weak separation / false negatives remain. Difficulty: unchanged encoder / sampling costs.
- **C: Three persistent interest slots — 5/7/8/6/7.** Originality: retention–activation separation / substantial precedent. Potential: recurring interests / unstable assignments. User alignment: preserves narrow preferences / slots may mix them. Model alignment: specialized states / indirect margin effect. Difficulty: compact memory / substantial integration.

**Selected: A**, prioritizing feasibility at 0% progress. Unlike the prior recent/full means, retrieve strictly preceding embeddings using agreement with the current interaction and recency. Unnormalized evidence mass controls reinforcement, preventing normalized attention from automatically giving an isolated weak match full weight.

```text
x = smoothly_normalized_item_embeddings(prefix)
a[t,s] = exp(-nonpadding_age(t,s)/10) * relu(dot(x[t],x[s]))², s<t
r[t] = sum_s a[t,s]*x[s] / (1 + sum_s a[t,s])
f[t] = SASRec(prefix)[t] + 2*sigmoid(theta)*r[t]
score(t,j) = dot(f[t], item_embedding[j])
```

Initialize amplitude to 0.01. This targets broad older associations outranking recent intent and unsupported extrapolation from isolated actions; it cannot establish compatibility or unmet needs. Compare baseline, A, and B within the shared budget. Preserve all routes, seeds, splits, diagnostic interfaces and predictor parity. Select exclusively by pinned macro validation HR@10; report no unmeasured gains.

idea.description: Add a bounded recent-anchor retrieval residual to each dataset-specific SASRec. At every causal position, use the current item embedding to retrieve similar, recent, strictly preceding interactions. Divide the weighted sum by one plus its unnormalized evidence mass, so weak support yields a weak correction rather than a full-strength normalized attention vector. Preserve the original candidate dot-product scorer.
idea.motivation: The selected intervention explicitly addresses two user-facing failures: broad older associations competing with recent narrow intent, and isolated interactions receiving unsupported preference reinforcement. Recency and current-item agreement select relevant preceding evidence; evidence-mass shrinkage limits the additional influence of weak matches. The original SASRec pathway remains responsible for learning legitimate new interests. The model-facing target is weak positive–negative separation, especially Electronics’ reported 14.95% wrong-ranking rate and −0.4812 lower-tail margin. Neither those training diagnostics nor the supplied historical aggregate scores establish a gain for this new mechanism. Retrieval evidence cannot establish ownership, compatibility, replacement needs, or purchase satisfaction.
idea.implementation_notes:
Use only training interaction histories in the initial experiment. Ignore the conflicting generic metadata examples: ratings, review text, categories, prices, stores and simulator traits are unavailable. Titles, descriptions and timestamps are permitted but unnecessary for this intervention.

Let e_t be the backbone item-table embedding before positional embeddings or dropout. Compute x_t=e_t/sqrt(sum(e_t²)+1e-4) in float32, with padding explicitly zeroed. For each nonpadding position t and strictly preceding nonpadding position s, define age as the difference between their cumulative nonpadding interaction indices. Set a_ts=exp(-age/10)*relu(dot(x_t,x_s))². Exclude t itself, future positions and padding. Define r_t=sum_s(a_ts*x_s)/(1+sum_s a_ts), and f_t=h_t+A*r_t, where h_t is the original SASRec feature and A=2*sigmoid(theta). Initialize theta=logit(0.005), giving A=0.01. No gate network or auxiliary loss is needed. Keep gradients through embeddings and retrieval weights. Serialize all constants.

The residual norm is below two because each x has norm at most one and the evidence denominator includes one. Candidate-logit changes remain dependent on candidate embedding norms. An empty preceding history gives exactly zero correction. One matching predecessor can contribute; the method attenuates weak support rather than certifying independent evidence. Repeated occurrences are not independent observations. Shared learned embeddings can reinforce popularity or spurious similarity, and recency decay can suppress legitimate long-range returns. Track these limitations rather than interpreting evidence mass as calibrated confidence.

Keep the backbone architecture, baseline sampled BCE, optimizer settings, negative sampler and training examples unchanged for A. Put theta in a parameter group without weight decay. Preserve the backbone initializer and training RNG streams where possible; initialize theta deterministically. Implement baseline mode as a complete branch bypass.

Retain DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], all four dataset routes, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and int(os.environ.get('SASREC_EPOCHS','200')). Save configuration, mappings, weights and logs beneath the trial directory. Keep each trial single-GPU. The predictor writer must emit the identical architecture, normalization, causal mask, amplitude and scoring logic.

Primary candidates are unchanged SASRec, retrieval residual A, and objective-only B. For B, use the official gSASRec gBCE formulation with K=32 and t=0.75 rather than inventing an approximation. Sample training-only negatives, excluding padding, the current target and known training-history positives; do not inspect held-out interactions. B changes both objective and negative count, so it is a practical alternative rather than an isolated causal test of calibration. A alone meets the selected idea’s two explicit user-failure mechanisms.

Allocate at most 12,000 GPU-seconds to each candidate’s four-category training bundle, split equally across categories, and reserve 7,200 GPU-seconds for all diagnostics, validation, parity checks, debugging and failures. Sum occupied GPU time across concurrent slots. Stop at the configured epoch limit or category time cap. Allow one schedule revision before comparative execution if baseline timing makes the allocation impractical. Use one terminal complete bundle per candidate for selection; avoid additional intermediate validation selection opportunities. Do not run C within this allocation.

Maintain DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. view.model must reference the actual complete trained module; view.item_emb remains the backbone item table. log2feats returns augmented B x L x D tensors and predict_score implements correctly broadcast dot products. Preserve user_train, meta_data and review_data without inventing missing fields. Compute original margin probes through the complete scorer. Add evidence mass, residual norm, amplitude, zero-support coverage and backbone-versus-augmented margins on identical valid positions. Define aggregation denominators and sample counts. Metadata category and review probes must report unavailable. Mean embedding cosine alone does not establish recommendation diversity or severe collapse.

Before training, verify strict-prefix causality, nonpadding-age calculation, empty and short histories, internal padding, finite gradients, bounded residuals and checkpoint reloads. Compare exported and training-path scores, including chunked full-catalog scoring, using atol=1e-5 and rtol=1e-4. Resolve top-10 disagreements and verify every dataset route. Keep host candidate generation and evaluation unchanged.

Run the required twenty-real-training-user, full-catalog unseen-item simulator protocol, five users per category. Track recent narrow matches and unsupported extrapolation separately from compatibility and satisfied-need failures. Select solely by the pinned four-category macro validation HR@10: 200 users/category, 99 unique negatives, evaluation seed 42. Exact ties prefer baseline, then A, then B. Record every attempt and its cost. Freeze the predictor before the host’s independent held-out evaluation. No experiments or improvement claims are made here.
idea.pseudocode:
DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']
epoch_limit = int(os.environ.get('SASREC_EPOCHS', '200'))

# Algorithm specification for integration with the existing baseline trainer.
for category in FOUR_CATEGORIES:
    model = baseline_SASRec_with_optional_retrieval(category)
    theta = Parameter(logit(0.005))

    def log2feats(sequence):
        h = backbone.log2feats(sequence)
        if mode == 'baseline':
            return h
        valid = sequence.ne(0)
        e = item_emb(sequence).float()
        x = e / sqrt(sum(e * e, dim=-1, keepdim=True) + 1e-4)
        x = x * valid[..., None]
        rank = cumsum(valid, dim=1)
        # Axes are batch, query position t, source position s.
        age = rank[:, :, None] - rank[:, None, :]
        allowed = strictly_lower_triangular_mask(sequence.length)
        allowed = allowed & valid[:, :, None] & valid[:, None, :]
        agreement = relu(matmul(x, transpose_last_two(x))) ** 2
        # Clamp before exp to avoid computing large masked future weights.
        weights = exp(-clamp(age, min=0).float() / 10.0)
        weights = weights * agreement * allowed
        mass = sum(weights, dim=-1, keepdim=True)
        residual = matmul(weights, x) / (1.0 + mass)
        features = h + (2.0 * sigmoid(theta) * residual).to(h.dtype)
        return features * valid[..., None]

    def predict_score(features, items):
        return correctly_broadcast_dot(features, item_emb(items))

    # A: unchanged baseline loss, optimizer, negatives and examples.
    # Baseline: bypass residual. B: unchanged backbone with official gBCE.
    train_to_configured_epoch_or_charged_time_cap()
    save_complete_checkpoint_and_configuration_under_trial_directory()
    write_predictor_using_identical_model_implementation()
    verify_causality_reload_routes_and_candidate_full_catalog_score_parity()
    run_compatible_diagnosis_and_required_training_user_simulator()

# Compare one terminal four-category bundle per candidate.
# Charge all GPU work and failures to the shared 43,200-second budget.
# Select exclusively through unchanged pinned macro validation HR@10.
# Freeze selected predictor before independent held-out evaluation.

originality.positive: Query-specific preceding-history retrieval with unnormalized evidence shrinkage creates a clear experimental distinction from the earlier fixed recent/full pooling residual.
originality.negative: Content attention, temporal decay, bounded residuals and support shrinkage are established techniques; their combination does not constitute a new model class.

future_potential.positive: Offers a compact framework for studying whether relevance-specific historical evidence improves current-intent ranking while retaining SASRec’s generalizing pathway.
future_potential.negative: Learned similarity is endogenous, repeated observations are dependent, and the mechanism cannot resolve practical compatibility or satisfied needs.

code_difficulty.positive: Uses standard masked matrix operations and one scalar parameter while preserving tensor features and dot-product inference.
code_difficulty.negative: Adds quadratic sequence retrieval, requires careful nonpadding chronology, and still needs diagnostic integration, compute accounting and predictor parity checks.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides the causal self-attention backbone and item dot-product scoring used by the baseline.
limitations: Does not explicitly constrain additional preference reinforcement using preceding-history evidence.
Interaction prediction does not verify practical compatibility or unmet needs.

related_work.title: gSASRec
contributions: Studies generalized BCE calibration and increased negative sampling while retaining SASRec.
Provides a strong objective-focused alternative for weak ranking separation.
limitations: Its reported findings do not identify the cause of Electronics’ supplied diagnostic margins.
Calibration does not identify false negatives or directly model supported current intent.

related_work.title: HyperHawkes
contributions: The supplied search summary describes latent-intent discovery, recurring-intent dynamics and short-term attention mixtures.
Motivates separating retained preferences from currently active interests.
limitations: A more elaborate intent model increases implementation and optimization cost.
The supplied evidence does not establish performance under this pinned benchmark.

related_work.title: Recformer
contributions: Combines textual item representations with sequential recommendation and pretraining.
The supplied search summary reports a weaker no-pretraining ablation.
limitations: Reported pretrained results do not establish gains for a randomly initialized text encoder under this task’s restrictions.
Textual similarity alone does not establish compatibility or purchase utility.

related_work.title: SCRM
contributions: The supplied search summary describes separate relationship graphs from click and purchase sequences with denoising and relationship constraints.
limitations: The required behavior distinctions are unavailable in the shared task.
Observed sequential association cannot be treated as a verified complement label.
